Keywords arrive in a suite two ways, both declared in `*** Settings ***`:

- **`Library`** imports Python-backed keywords — the standard libraries
  (`Collections`, `String`, `OperatingSystem`, …) and third-party ones.
- **`Resource`** imports keywords and variables from a shared `.resource`
  file you write in Robot Framework syntax.

This chapter's workspace already has a resource at `resources/common.resource`
imported by `checks/imports.robot`. Add a **library** import alongside it.

## Task 1 — Import the Collections library and use one of its keywords

**Goal:** in `checks/imports.robot`, import the `Collections` library and add a
test that builds a list and checks its length.

Here is the same pattern with a different library — importing `String` and
calling one of its keywords. Adapt it to Collections.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library    String

*** Test Cases ***
Path Splits Into Parts
    @{parts}=    Split String    a/b/c    /
    Length Should Be    ${parts}    3
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** `checks/imports.robot` imports `Collections` and calls `Create List`,
and the new test passes.

<!-- hint -->
Add `Library    Collections` to the `*** Settings ***` section, alongside the
existing `Resource` import.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Add a test that builds a list with `Create List` and checks it with
`Length Should Be`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
`${items}=    Create List    backpack    lamp    mug`, then
`Length Should Be    ${items}    3`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Resource     ../resources/common.resource
Library      Collections

*** Test Cases ***
Catalog List Has Items
    ${items}=    Create List    backpack    lamp    mug
    Length Should Be    ${items}    3
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run the suite green

Run it:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

**Check:** the test `Catalog List Has Items` passes.
